run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T04:32:48Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained at the mechanism level: from ~04:08:41 onward frontend-proxy began recording ERROR spans on its server span 'ingress' (zero in the 60 minutes before 04:08), and its access log shows the failing requests are HTTP 503 with response flags UC and response-code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on the 'frontend' upstream (Service 100.71.53.109:8080, single endpoint pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2), i.e. the frontend peer terminated the connection before sending response headers. 20.29 error spans accumulated over 70 minutes against 24,771 NON-ERROR (UNSET) ingress spans; the proxy's client-side 'router frontend egress' span shows zero ERROR in the whole window. All 11 sampled 503 lines are on product-catalog-backed GET routes (/api/products/{productId}, /api/data). The frontend itself shows no own failure evidence: 0 ERROR spans, flat p95 (157.9 ms at 03:42:48 vs 99.7-150 ms later), memory 121-131.6 MB against a 200Mi limit, unchanged CPU-throttling rate at the onset, 0 restarts, ready pod, and no stdout/stderr lines at all. No other service shows a new error or latency anomaly; the flagd EventStream ERROR spans on ad/fraud-detection/recommendation pre-date the onset. The load-generator rollout at 04:23:38-39 happened after the first 503 (04:08:41) and is not the trigger. Why the frontend side terminates these connections is not established by the available evidence: Jaeger data stops at 04:06:06, the frontend emits no logs, and the Envoy configuration is not readable from a configmap.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans are new at ~04:08-04:09: the 5-minute rate of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} is 0 at samples 04:03:48-04:08:48, becomes 0.0037 spans/s at 04:09:48, peaks at 0.0259 spans/s at 04:15:48 and reads 0.0111 spans/s at 04:27:48 - the same value reported as the alert's current error rate.

Over the 70-minute query window the frontend-proxy 'ingress' counters increased by 20.294 ERROR spans against 24,771.0 UNSET spans, so the alert rests on a small but newly present error fraction of proxy traffic.

Baseline check: increase over the 60 minutes ending 04:08:00 was exactly 0 for both frontend-proxy ERROR series that exist (span_name="ingress", SPAN_KIND_SERVER and span_name="router frontend egress", SPAN_KIND_CLIENT), confirming no error spans were recorded before ~04:08.

Errors are recorded only on the server span: 'ingress' (STATUS_CODE_ERROR) carries the errors while the client span 'router frontend egress' has a 5-minute ERROR rate of 0 in every sample of the window.

frontend-proxy access logs for 04:08:41-04:13:17 contain six failing requests, all of the exact form '"GET /api/products/{id}|/api/data/... HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} ... 0 95 ...' with upstream cluster 'frontend', UPSTREAM_HOST 100.71.53.109:8080 and client user agent python-requests/2.32.5 - e.g. at 04:08:41.642, 04:11:23.206, 04:11:23.626, 04:12:49.779, 04:13:17.388, 04:13:17.572.

The same 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses on cluster 'frontend' continue later in the window: five more at 04:30:52.988, 04:31:09.066, 04:32:22.569, 04:34:14.998 and 04:36:27.650, all with 95 response bytes and no upstream service time.

The failing upstream is the frontend Service: Service frontend has clusterIP 100.71.53.109 (port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend), matching the UPSTREAM_HOST 100.71.53.109:8080 in the 503 lines, and Endpoints 'frontend' has exactly one address, 100.96.2.93 (pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2).

Neither pod crashed or was replaced during the window: frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 (start 03:51:50Z) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth (start 03:51:49Z) are Running/ready with restartCount 0, and deployments frontend and frontend-proxy report available=1, ready=1, updated=1.

frontend container memory working set rose only from 121,044,992 bytes at 04:02:48 to 131,592,192 bytes at 04:42:48 against its 200Mi limit, and frontend-proxy stayed at ~20.3-20.9 MB against its 50Mi limit; no approach to the limits is visible across the onset.

CPU CFS throttling shows no step at the 04:08 onset: frontend's rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total[5m]) is ~4.5-5.8 across 03:42-04:42 (0.81 at 03:35, 5.34 at 03:40, 5.0 at 04:13, 4.63 at 04:37) and frontend-proxy's is ~0.10-1.09 throughout; both were already throttled before the errors began.

The frontend service recorded no ERROR spans of its own in the window (its ERROR increase is 0 for GET, POST, /api/cart, /api/data, /api/products, /api/recommendations, checkout and the grpc client spans), and its p95 for 'GET /api/products/{productId}' was 157.9 ms at 03:42:48 and 99.7-150 ms at the later 5-minute steps - no latency degradation after the onset.

No other service shows a latency anomaly over the window: p95 by service is flat (product-catalog 1.92-1.95 ms, quote 1.90-1.94 ms, cart 51.6-99.0 ms, recommendation 28.7-84.9 ms, checkout 105-180 ms, accounting 3558-4063 ms, i.e. accounting's high value is its pre-existing level at the earliest sample too).

The ERROR spans on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation are flagd streaming spans that already existed before the onset: at 04:08:00 the 60-minute increase was 1.152 for recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' (and 0 for ad/fraud Resolve* series), and over the later 70 minutes they total only 3.05 (ad EventStream), 3.05 (fraud-detection EventStream) and 4.06 (recommendation EventStream).

The load-generator rollout happened after the first 503: at 04:23:38-04:23:39 replica set load-generator-57ffcd644 was scaled 1->0 and its pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 deleted while replica set load-generator-84895ffcd was scaled 0->1 and pod load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb created; both ReplicaSets use the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-load-generator and identical env (LOCUST_USERS=50, LOCUST_HOST=http://frontend-proxy:8080).

Only span-derived metrics exist for frontend-proxy in this Prometheus - traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket - so there is no HTTP-level request/error metric (no http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series) to cross-check the 503 rate.

Jaeger's available spans do not cover the error period: the 40 spans retrieved from the stored frontend-proxy search slice all start at 04:06:03 and carry status tag http.status_code 200, and the slice's data_as_of is 2026-11-15T04:06:06, while the first 503 is at 04:08:41.

The frontend container has no readinessProbe and no livenessProbe configured (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend, limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi), so probe-driven endpoint flapping is not a mechanism available in this deployment.

Best supported explanation of the alert: frontend-proxy is returning 503 because the frontend peer closes/resets an established upstream connection before response headers (an HTTP/1.1 upstream connection-reuse / keep-alive termination between Envoy and the Next.js frontend). This fits the exact Envoy detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, the absence of any upstream service time on those lines, zero ERROR on the proxy's own 'router frontend egress' span, and the complete absence of frontend-side error, latency, memory, throttling or restart signals; it is not proven because the Envoy upstream timeout/keep-alive settings and the frontend's server keep-alive behaviour could not be read.

Alternative unresolved candidate: the termination is tied to the frontend's product-catalog-backed routes. All 11 sampled 503 lines are GET /api/products/{productId} or GET /api/data (the routes that render product data), which is suggestive, but the sample is small and product-catalog's own p95 stayed at 1.92-1.95 ms with no ERROR series returned, so no failure in that dependency was observed and this remains unproven.

Rejected as the trigger: frontend resource exhaustion / OOM. The frontend pod has restartCount 0 with an empty lastState, memory stayed at 121-131.6 MB of a 200Mi limit, and its CPU-throttling rate was already ~5 before the 04:08 onset and did not change - no resource step coincides with the first 503 at 04:08:41.

Rejected as the trigger: frontend-proxy itself becoming saturated. Its memory held at ~20.3-20.9 MB of 50Mi and its throttling rate stayed within 0.10-1.09 across the onset, and the response-code detail attributes the failure to the upstream connection being terminated, not to proxy-side resource pressure.

Rejected as the trigger: the load-generator rollout at 04:23:38. The first 503 line is at 04:08:41, about 15 minutes earlier, and the old and new load-generator ReplicaSets have identical image and environment, so the rollout is a change inside the window that did not start this error episode.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the flagd EventStream ERROR spans on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation. They were already being counted before the onset (recommendation's EventStream shows 1.152 errors in the 60 minutes ending 04:08:00) and they are attributed to those services, not to frontend-proxy, whose own error series was 0 in that baseline.

To confirm or refute the keep-alive hypothesis, compare the Envoy cluster 'frontend' upstream HTTP options (idle_timeout / max_requests_per_connection / upstream keepalive) with the Next.js frontend's Node server keep-alive settings (server.keepAliveTimeout, headersTimeout), and align the upstream idle timeout below the frontend's close timeout.

Enable and collect the frontend container's application/access logging (it currently emits no stdout/stderr lines) and, if possible, Envoy debug logs or upstream_rq/upstream_cx counters for cluster 'frontend', so the direction and timing of the connection termination can be observed directly instead of inferred from response flags.

gaps: No error traces could be inspected: Jaeger's newest data in this target ended at 2026-11-15T04:06:06 while the first 503 is at 04:08:41, so the span graph (and parent/child edges) of the failing requests is unknown.
The frontend container produced no stdout/stderr lines at all in the windows read (04:00-04:20 and 04:30-04:32:30), so the Node.js server side of the terminated connections could not be observed.

frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration is not available as a readable object (only configmaps flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector, product-catalog-products exist), so upstream keep-alive/idle timeout settings and retry policy could not be verified.

The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate was not found in Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no data), so its exact expression, threshold and evaluation labels are unknown; the alert payload was treated only as a lead.

Pod log reads hit the 4 MiB read limit: 503 lines between 04:13:17-04:30:52 and after 04:37:34 were not read, so the complete set and per-route distribution of the 503s is only partially known (11 lines sampled).

All observed client traffic carries the python-requests user agent of the load-generator (LOCUST_HOST=http://frontend-proxy:8080); no real user or browser traffic was observed, so customer impact is unverified.

What changed at the 03:51:48-03:51:50 creation of every otel-demo pod (including frontend and frontend-proxy) is unknown: older ReplicaSets for those deployments no longer exist and the change_history integration is not available, so an image/configuration change preceding the 04:08 onset cannot be ruled in or out.

kube_pod_status_ready series for the frontend pod returned no data, so readiness history cannot be checked; no Evicted/OOMKilled/Unhealthy events were returned for otel-demo, but events expire and absence is not proof.

ERROR-status series were not returned at all for cart, checkout, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping and image-provider, so their error state is unknown rather than zero; only their latency and the absence of a new error step were checked.
next_steps: Inspect the Envoy bootstrap/route configuration used by frontend-proxy (image-baked) for the 'frontend' cluster's upstream HTTP protocol options, timeouts and keep-alive settings, and compare them with the frontend's Node keepAliveTimeout/headersTimeout.
Capture a short tcpdump or Envoy debug-log window on frontend-proxy (node i-0ec8b1fcc1cb45b42) during a reproduced 503 to see which side sends the FIN/RST and at what request phase.

Enable request logging in the frontend container (currently silent) and correlate the failing x-request-id values (e.g. 95bc46c3-f5bd-98f9-8bf1-cc1869f3fe40, 492c0538-5931-95e1-a522-f572d5efb857) with frontend-side handling.

Track whether the 503 UC rate scales with keep-alive idle churn by testing a client that opens fresh connections versus one that reuses them, without changing the production workload during the observation.
